summary: This note describes Chandi Devi Temple, a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Chandi Devi in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, India. It sits atop Neel Parvat on the Eastern summit of the Sivalik Hills. The note says the temple was built in 1929 by Suchat Singh, while the main murti is said to have been installed in the 8th century by Adi Shankaracharya. The temple is also called Neel Parvat Teerth and is one of the Panch Tirth pilgrimages in Haridwar.
one_line: Chandi Devi Temple is a Hindu temple atop Neel Parvat in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, dedicated to Goddess Chandi Devi and counted among Haridwar's Panch Tirth pilgrimages.
key_facts: Chandi Devi Temple, Haridwar is a Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Chandi Devi.
Chandi Devi Temple is located in the holy city of Haridwar in the Uttarakhand state of India.
The Chandi Devi Temple is situated atop the Neel Parvat on the Eastern summit of the Sivalik Hills.
The Sivalik Hills are described in the note as the southernmost mountain chain of the Himalayas.
Chandi Devi Temple was built in 1929 by Suchat Singh during his reign as the King of Kashmir.
The main murti of Chandi Devi at Chandi Devi Temple is said to have been installed in the 8th century.
The main murti of Chandi Devi is said to have been installed by Adi Shankaracharya, described as one of the greatest priests of Hindu religion.
Chandi Devi Temple is also known as Neel Parvat Teerth.
Chandi Devi Temple is one of the "Panch Tirth" (Five Pilgrimages) located within Haridwar.
